description: The Fire Goat in Chinese astrology: personality, Fire element traits, 1967 and 2027 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Fire Goat is the Goat born in a Fire year, one of five versions of the eighth animal. It combines the Goat's gentleness with Fire's qualities. Fire Goat years between 1924 and 2044 are 1967 and 2027. The Goat's fixed element is Earth.

sections.heading: The Fire Goat personality
paragraphs: Fire generates Earth, and the Goat's fixed element is Earth, so a Fire stem is said to warm and strengthen the Goat, adding confidence and expressiveness to its gentle nature. Fire Goats are often portrayed as creative, passionate and charming, more willing than other Goats to step into the spotlight. They tend to have strong artistic instincts and a flair for presentation. Their warmth draws people to them, and they often have wide social circles. The supporting flow lifts the Goat's spirits, though it can also intensify emotions, and Fire Goats may swing between enthusiasm and discouragement, or react strongly when they feel unappreciated or misunderstood. Beauty, for a Fire Goat, is something to share loudly rather than admire alone.

Belonging to the south and to the height of summer, Fire brings brightness, drive and visibility to any sign it colours. Classical texts connect it with enthusiasm, leadership and the urge to be seen and to make an impression. A Fire stem tends to make an animal more expressive, more daring and more openly emotional than its usual reputation suggests. People born in Fire years are often described as inspiring company and natural motivators. The caution most readings attach is a short fuse and a difficulty with slow seasons, when steady effort matters more than spark and the reward is a long way off.

sections.heading: Fire Goat at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Fire is usually linked with initiative, persuasion and visible leadership. Fire-year people are often described as the ones who launch things, pitch ideas and keep morale high when a deadline looms, which suits performance, sales, media, entrepreneurship and campaigning of every kind. They tend to thrive on momentum and recognition. The traditional caution concerns stamina and follow-through: a Fire stem may lose patience with routine detail, so pairing with methodical colleagues and pacing energy across a project usually helps.

The Fire Goat brings flair and unexpected courage to a sign usually known for gentleness. Performance, fashion, visual arts, events and creative direction suit it, since expressive talent there can be seen and celebrated. It works best with encouragement and a clear brief, and it may lose heart in environments that dismiss its ideas out of hand. In love, the Fire Goat is romantic, warm and dramatic, drawn to grand gestures and memorable dates. It needs reassurance and admiration as well as a stable home to return to. The usual friction is emotional weather: sudden moods, hurt feelings and impulsive spending, especially when it feels insecure about where the relationship is heading.

sections.heading: Fire Goat years and dates
paragraphs: The table from 1924 to 2044 holds 2 Fire Goat years: 1967, starting Feb 9 and 2027, starting Feb 6. Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1967 anyone born before Feb 9 is a Fire Horse, not a Fire Goat. It takes sixty years for the Fire stem and the Goat branch to coincide again, which is why the same pairing marks grandparents and grandchildren rather than siblings. Every Fire Goat year is Yin, matching the Goat's own polarity.

In the sexagenary calendar this is the Ding-Wei year, the Fire stem Ding with the Goat's branch Wei. Births just before each new year fall in the Fire Horse year (before February 9, 1967) and the Fire Horse year (before February 6, 2027), and births in the weeks after each Fire Goat year ends belong to the Earth Monkey. The new year itself fell on a Thursday in 1967 and Saturday in 2027.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Fire Goat
paragraphs: Emotional steadiness is usually the Fire Goat's richest area of growth. Noticing early signs of overwhelm, and taking time out before reacting, keeps moods from colouring decisions. Because they invest deeply in creative work, they may take criticism personally; separating their worth from any single project helps. Fire Goats often benefit from routines that ground their energy, such as regular exercise or cooking. Surrounding themselves with encouraging but honest friends suits them well. Sharing their talents through teaching or performance gives their warmth a lasting outlet. Balanced, Fire Goats bring beauty and joy wherever they go.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Fire Goat shares the Goat's San He trine with the Rabbit and Pig (the Wood trine), its Liu He bond with the Horse, and its Liu Chong clash with the Ox. The element adds a second layer: another Fire sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Fire in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Fire Goat years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1967 (from February 9, 1967) and 2027 (from February 6, 2027). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Fire Goat's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Fire and the Goat's fixed element is Earth; in the five-element cycles fire generates Earth. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Fire Goat?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Rabbit and Pig (San He) and the Horse (Liu He). The Ox is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Fire Goat called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Ding-Wei. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Fire stem Ding, followed by its earthly branch, here Wei for the Goat, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Fire Goat different from other Goats?
faq.answer: All Goats share gentleness, creativity and empathy. The Fire year element changes the tone: fire is the element of summer and full daylight, and a Fire year is traditionally said to turn up the volume of whatever animal it meets.
